source: When we look at the most common words in the dataset, it’s what you’d expect: “Stop” is the #1 word in the dataset, appearing 1,304,417 times, followed by “One way.”
claim: The most common term is “stop” with 1,304,417 mentions, followed by “one way” with 1,145,477.

source: First, here are the most common words, as well as phrases in our data (the algorithm identified phrases if they appeared as a single line of text).
claim: The 50 most common terms rank from “stop” (1st, 1,304,417) and “one way” (2nd, 1,145,477) down to “truck” (49th, 80,566) and “for rent” (50th, 79,880).

source: As expected, many of these are related to driving, traffic, and street signs, words that you’d find on any streetscape in the US.
claim: 32 of the 50 most common terms are flagged as street-sign words.

source: Let’s filter these out, as well as common filler words (as, the, is, of, etc.), so we can explore the more surprising terms that appear in NYC.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, the ranking runs from “no” (1st, 482,811), “open” (2nd, 228,737) and “atm” (3rd, 211,704) to “no fee” (1,500th, 4,251).

source: Fedders, at #25, is the logo of an A/C brand that had their units built into the exterior of buildings, from the 1950s to the 1990s, as through-the-wall slots.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “fedders” ranks 25th with 70,687 mentions.

source: At #102 is Yodock, a brand of orange and white plastic barriers, often seen in make-shift sidewalks around construction areas.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “yodock” ranks 102nd with 29,791 mentions.

source: Acars (at #253) is actually “4cars,” misread by the algorithm for translating text in images.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “acars” ranks 253rd with 16,049 mentions.

source: Nathan’s might have the hot dog brand cachet, but Sabrett (ranking 293rd) has the territory, with carts in most NYC tourist traps.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “sabrett” ranks 293rd with 14,194 mentions.

source: NYC is home to largest Muslim community in the United States, so it’s no surprise to see halal— food prepared according to Islamic dietary law—ranked at #304.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “halal” ranks 304th with 13,646 mentions.

source: Siamese (#350) refers to a type of hose connection for firefighters.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “siamese” ranks 350th with 12,134 mentions.

source: Earlier, we depicted the geography of beware (#383), which is concentrated in residential areas fortunate enough to have lawns and fencing. Here we see how popular the phrase is, ranking in the top 1,000.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “beware” ranks 383rd with 11,192 mentions.

source: In case you didn’t already know (as evidenced by this project), you’re always under surveillance (#492) in NYC.
claim: After excluding street-sign terms, “surveillance” ranks 492nd with 9,650 mentions.
